acceptance: Speech Blocks can generate reviewable narrator-and-character blocks from direct LLM text responses, preserves aligned source slices, flags gaps/unmatched/unknown output for operator review, falls back only failed segments, splits large dialogue-heavy chunks before model output becomes too large, resumes after completed segments, and no longer emits a whole-chunk narrator fallback for chunk-0033-style failures.
assumptions: Use the recommended source policy: preserve original source text where aligned and mark uncertainty for review rather than trusting unmatched LLM text.
Use the recommended failure policy: save deterministic narrator review fallback for only the failed segment and continue.
No compatibility migration is required for old atomic/source-span operation state or old repair responses.

scope: In scope: prompt/schema replacement, direct block normalization, source-text alignment and review flags, segment-level fallback, output-aware segmentation, segment-level resume/cancel state, relevant tests, requirements, and component documentation. Out of scope: backward compatibility with old atomic/source-span responses or checkpoints, UI redesign beyond existing edit/review surfaces, changing Audio Blocks or Audio Assembly contracts except through existing Speech Blocks outputs, and packaging/release work.
alignment.understanding: Replace narrator-and-character Speech Blocks generation with an operator-review direct LLM block-splitting contract. The LLM will return ordered blocks containing text, speaker_id, content_kind, confidence, and warning_flags. AudioMancer will preserve source text where returned text can be aligned, mark uncertainty for review, fall back only the failed segment, split large chunks by output-safety limits, and keep generation interruptible/resumable at segment granularity. This is a breaking replacement for the atomic/source-span selection and repair contract; old operation checkpoints do not need migration.

intent.statement: Replace Speech Blocks narrator-and-character generation with an operator-review direct LLM block-splitting contract that preserves source text where aligned, flags uncertain output for review, uses segment-level fallback instead of whole-chunk atomic fallback, and remains interruptible and resumable.

examples: A segment containing narration and quoted speech yields ordered reviewable Speech Blocks with original source text preserved where aligned.
spec_items.statement: Narrator-and-character Speech Blocks generation accepts direct LLM blocks with text, speaker_id, content_kind, confidence, and warning_flags, aligns returned text to the source segment, persists aligned source slices, marks uncertainty for review, and never persists unmatched invented model text as trusted audiobook text.

examples: One malformed response in a multi-segment chunk creates a speech_blocks_ai_parse_failed block for that segment while later segment responses are still normalized.
spec_items.statement: If a direct Speech Blocks LLM response is malformed or unusable, generation persists deterministic narrator needs_review fallback blocks only for that failed segment and continues with later segments instead of falling back the whole chunk.

examples: After cancellation following segment 0, resume skips segment 0 and calls the provider for segment 1.
spec_items.statement: Direct Speech Blocks generation persists segment-level progress, honors cooperative cancellation between provider calls and segment persistence, resumes from the next unfinished segment, and restarts incompatible old atomic/source-span checkpoints rather than migrating them.

examples: A chunk larger than the output-safety cap is sent as multiple direct-block LLM requests.
spec_items.statement: Narrator-and-character Speech Blocks generation splits source chunks into contiguous LLM request segments using an output-safety source budget capped around 2000 estimated source tokens, even when the selected profile permits larger input.
